types.name: EntityType
types.description:
Known entity types across all integrated products.
Additional types may appear in the 'entityType' string field.

types.name: String
types.description: The `String` scalar type represents textual data, represented as UTF-8 character sequences. The String type is most often used by GraphQL to represent free-form human-readable text.

types.name: EntitiesFilterInput
types.description: Filters for listing entities

types.name: TopologyOptionsInput
types.description:
Options for traversing the topology graph from a given entity.
Controls direction and depth of traversal.

types.name: Boolean
types.description: The `Boolean` scalar type represents `true` or `false`.

types.name: TopologyFilterInput
types.description: Filters for the standalone entityTopology query

types.name: Entity
types.description:
A resource or component discovered by any integrated product
(Turbonomic, Instana, Concert, SevOne, NS1, etc.)

fields.name: className
fields.description: The entity class as reported by the source product (e.g. 'VirtualMachine', 'Image', 'BusinessApplication')

fields.name: entityType
fields.description: Alias for className - the type of this entity

fields.name: discoveredBy
fields.description: The product or probe that discovered this entity

fields.name: externalIds
fields.description: External IDs assigned by other products (e.g. Instana service ID, Concert build artifact ID)

fields.name: cves
fields.description: CVE vulnerabilities associated with this entity (available for Image entities when Concert is configured)

fields.name: actions
fields.description: Turbonomic actions for this entity. Returns recommended actions like resize, move, scale, etc.

fields.name: topology
fields.description: Traverse the topology graph from this entity to find related entities

types.name: ID
types.description: The `ID` scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as `"4"`) or integer (such as `4`) input value will be accepted as an ID.

types.name: Int
types.description: The `Int` scalar type represents non-fractional signed whole numeric values. Int can represent values between -(2^31) and 2^31 - 1.

types.name: Float
types.description: The `Float` scalar type represents signed double-precision fractional values as specified by [IEEE 754](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IEEE_floating_point).

types.name: ExternalIds

fields.name: source
fields.description: The product or probe that assigned this ID (e.g. 'Concert', 'Instana', 'ibmdevsandbox-instanaibm.instana.io')

fields.name: externalId
fields.description: The ID used by that product for this entity

types.name: EntityAspects
types.description:
Entity aspects provide additional metadata about entities beyond their core properties.

IMPORTANT: Not all aspects are available for all entities. Each aspect type only applies to
specific entity classes, and even within those classes, individual properties may be null
depending on the entity's configuration, cloud provider, or discovery method.

Always check for null values when accessing aspect properties.

fields.name: virtualMachineAspect
fields.description:
Virtual machine aspect - applies to VirtualMachine entities.
Properties may vary based on hypervisor type and cloud provider.

fields.name: storageAspect
fields.description:
Storage aspect - applies to Storage, DiskArray, LogicalPool, StorageController, and StorageTier entities.
Properties may vary based on storage type and vendor.

fields.name: applicationServiceAspect
fields.description:
Cloud PaaS application service aspect (e.g., Azure App Service, AWS Elastic Beanstalk, GCP App Engine).
This aspect applies to Service entities that host applications, not to Application entities themselves.
Properties may vary based on cloud provider and service configuration.

types.name: VirtualMachineAspect
types.description:
Virtual machine aspect containing VM-specific metadata.

NOTE: Not all properties are available for all VMs. Property availability depends on:
- Hypervisor type (VMware, Hyper-V, KVM, etc.)
- Cloud provider (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.)
- Discovery method and agent installation
- VM configuration and features enabled

Always check for null values before using these properties.

fields.name: numVCPUs
fields.description: Number of virtual CPUs allocated to the VM

fields.name: guestOS
fields.description: Guest operating system name (e.g., 'Ubuntu 20.04', 'Windows Server 2019')

fields.name: ipAddress
fields.description: List of IP addresses assigned to the VM

fields.name: macAddress
fields.description: List of MAC addresses for the VM's network interfaces

fields.name: creationTimeStamp
fields.description: Timestamp when the VM was created

fields.name: coresPerSocketRatio
fields.description: Ratio of CPU cores per socket (relevant for NUMA and licensing)

fields.name: agentMode
fields.description: Agent mode indicating the level of monitoring (e.g., 'full', 'guest')

fields.name: ebsOptimized
fields.description: Whether EBS optimization is enabled (AWS-specific)

fields.name: ahubLicense
fields.description: Whether Azure Hybrid Use Benefit (AHUB) license is applied

fields.name: vendorToolsVersion
fields.description: Version of vendor tools installed (e.g., VMware Tools version)

fields.name: vgpuProfile
fields.description: vGPU profile assigned to the VM (e.g., 'grid_m60-1q')

fields.name: resourceId
fields.description: Cloud provider resource identifier

fields.name: hardwareVersion
fields.description: Hardware version of the VM (e.g., 'vmx-13' for VMware)

fields.name: vendorLink
fields.description: Direct link to the VM in the vendor's management console

fields.name: passthroughGPUIds
fields.description: List of PCI passthrough GPU device IDs

fields.name: passthroughGPUModels
fields.description: List of PCI passthrough GPU model names

fields.name: minimumHosts
fields.description: Minimum number of hosts required for VM placement (anti-affinity rules)

fields.name: flavorName
fields.description: Cloud instance type or flavor name (e.g., 't2.micro', 'Standard_D2s_v3')

types.name: StorageAspect
types.description:
Storage aspect containing storage-specific metadata.

NOTE: Not all properties are available for all storage entities. Property availability depends on:
- Storage type (SAN, NAS, HCI, Cloud storage, etc.)
- Storage vendor and model
- Discovery method and API capabilities
- Storage configuration and features

Always check for null values before using these properties.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Display name of the storage entity

fields.name: externalNames
fields.description: List of external names for the storage

fields.name: technologyType
fields.description: HCI technology type (e.g., 'VSAN')

fields.name: redundancyMethod
fields.description: Redundancy method (e.g., 'RAID_1', 'RAID_5', 'ERASURE_CODING')

fields.name: failuresToTolerate
fields.description: Number of failures the storage can tolerate

fields.name: spaceReservationPct
fields.description: Space reservation percentage for the storage policy

fields.name: minimumHosts
fields.description: Minimum number of hosts required

fields.name: rawCapacity
fields.description: Raw capacity in GB

fields.name: rawFreespace
fields.description: Raw free space in GB

fields.name: rawUncommitted
fields.description: Raw uncommitted space in GB

fields.name: isHciStorage
fields.description: Whether this is HCI (Hyper-Converged Infrastructure) storage

fields.name: vendorLink
fields.description: Direct link to the storage in the vendor's management console

fields.name: storageCluster
fields.description: Storage cluster name

types.name: ApplicationServiceAspect
types.description:
Cloud Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) application service aspect.
Applies to Service entities that host applications in cloud environments.
Examples: Azure App Service, AWS Elastic Beanstalk, GCP App Engine.

This is NOT for generic Application entities - it's specifically for
cloud PaaS services that can host multiple applications with scaling capabilities.

NOTE: Not all properties are available for all services. Property availability depends on:
- Cloud provider (Azure, AWS, GCP, etc.)
- Service type and tier
- Service configuration and features enabled
- Discovery method and API capabilities

Always check for null values before using these properties.

fields.name: maxInstanceCount
fields.description: Maximum number of instances allowed for this service

fields.name: instanceCount
fields.description: Current number of running instances of this service

fields.name: platform
fields.description: Platform type (e.g., 'LINUX', 'WINDOWS', 'DOCKER')

fields.name: tier
fields.description: Service tier (e.g., 'BASIC', 'STANDARD', 'PREMIUM')

fields.name: appCount
fields.description: Number of unique applications running on this service

fields.name: zoneRedundant
fields.description: Whether zone redundancy is enabled for high availability

fields.name: daysEmpty
fields.description: Number of days the service has been empty/unused

fields.name: resourceId
fields.description: Cloud provider resource identifier (e.g., Azure resource ID, AWS ARN, GCP full resource name)

fields.name: errorBudgetRemaining

fields.name: totalErrorBudget

fields.name: entities
fields.description:
List entities with optional filtering and pagination.
Results are filtered based on the authenticated user's access permissions.

fields.name: entity
fields.description:
Get a single entity by UUID.
Returns null if the entity does not exist or the user does not have access.

fields.name: resolveEntity
fields.description:
Resolve an entity from any product identifier.
Accepts a Turbonomic UUID, an Instana service ID, a Concert build artifact ID,
or any other external ID known to the platform.

Resolution strategy:
1. Try as a Turbonomic UUID directly (fast path)
2. If not found, search all entities by external/vendor ID (cross-product lookup)

Returns the entity with all its known identifiers across all integrated products
via the 'externalIds' field.

fields.name: entityDetails
fields.description: Get extended details for an entity (experimental)

fields.name: entityActions
fields.description: Get recommended actions for a specific entity

fields.name: entityStats
fields.description: Get statistics/metrics for an entity over a time range

fields.name: entityActionStats
fields.description: Get action statistics for an entity over a time range

fields.name: entityTags
fields.description: Get tags associated with an entity

fields.name: entityTopology
fields.description:
Traverse the topology graph for an entity to find related entities.
Use the 'entity' query with the 'topology' field for inline traversal.

fields.name: impactedApplications
fields.description:
Find applications impacted by a specific CVE.
Requires Concert integration to be configured.
Traverses: CVE → Concert build artifacts → Images (via externalIds) → topology → Applications

fields.name: applications
fields.description:
Get applications from Instana with performance metrics.
Health information is enriched from Turbonomic when available.

fields.name: application
fields.description:
Get a single application from Instana by ID with performance metrics.
Health information is enriched from Turbonomic when available.

fields.name: health
fields.description: Health check endpoint

fields.name: createEntityTags
fields.description: Create tags for an entity

fields.name: deleteEntityTags
fields.description: Delete tags from an entity

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description: Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description: A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a __DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.
